verdict: Back to winning ways at Palace. Szoboszlai's knee is the worry.

posters.headline: Reds beat Palace 3-1 at Selhurst
posters.summary: Mac Allister, Wirtz and Isak scored. Nketiah got a late penalty. Liverpool climb to fourth on 18 points.

read.what: Mac Allister headed in a Szoboszlai free-kick in the first half. Wirtz made it 2-0 early in the second (54' per NBC Sports). Isak scored in the 89th minute. Nketiah scored a stoppage-time penalty. A Strand Larsen goal for Palace was ruled out for offside. Sources differ on the minute of the first goal.
read.context: It ended two straight defeats, Iraola's first back-to-back losses as Liverpool manager. Liverpool have 18 points from 10 games, three behind City and four behind Brighton. Palace are bottom.
read.take: Opinion: a deserved result, but the first half was shaky and Alisson made key saves. Three points matter more than the style. Watch whether the midfield balance holds against stronger sides.

posters.headline: Szoboszlai doubtful, knee issue
posters.summary: Iraola says Szoboszlai hyper-extended his knee and was not 100%. Hungary duty is in doubt.

read.what: Iraola said Szoboszlai hyper-extended the knee a little and was not 100 per cent. He said the player will want to join Hungary and that both clubs' medical staff will assess him. No scan result or timeline has been given.
read.context: Szoboszlai set up the first goal and went off in the second half. Liverpool face Man United on 22 Nov, so the break gives time to recover if he rests.
read.take: Opinion: the injury looks minor so far, but it is unproven. Watch whether Hungary use him. Iraola's preference to avoid a repeat of the last break is a hint he would rather he stayed.

stories.headline: Palace expected to sack Sage, Frank favourite
stories.summary: Palace are bottom after a seventh league defeat. Sky Sports names Thomas Frank as leading candidate. No decision yet.

read.what: Sky Sports says Sage is likely to be sacked and Frank is the leading contender. Dyche, Lampard and others are also on Palace's list. Jamie Carragher expects Sage to go before the next game. Nothing is confirmed by the club.
read.context: Sage replaced Glasner in the summer. Palace face Liverpool's rivals after the break with a new manager possible.
read.take: Opinion: a sacking looks likely but is a report, not a fact, until Palace confirm it.

talking.headline: Late Palace penalty and long VAR check
talking.summary: Referee Harrington gave a stoppage-time penalty for Kerkez and Osorio. Iraola was very upset.
talking.for: Palace: there was contact in the box when Kerkez and Osorio jumped for the header, and the referee pointed to the spot.
talking.against: Iraola: it was a clash of heads, both players went for the ball, and similar contact in Palace's box is not given. He said the VAR check took a long time.
talking.take: Opinion: it cost a clean sheet, not points, so it is a grumble not a grievance. No official explanation was published in the sources I opened.
